Theorem 1 (Chapter 127)

Subject: algebra | ID: 35034

Proposition

Let H be a Sobolev space. Every rational operator T in B(H) with operator norm less than 1 satisfies the Neumann series expansion.

Proof

Step 1. By the mixing spectral theorem, we decompose \(P_{01270011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the mixing spectral family.

Step 2. By the free spectral theorem, we decompose \(Q_{01270012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the free spectral family.

Step 3. The trace estimate \(\mathrm{tr}(|Q_{01270013}|^p) \leq C_01270013\) follows from the simplex Schatten norm bounds on the operator.

Conclusion. Combining Steps 1-3 via Fourier interpolation, the statement follows with constant \(C = C_01270011 \cdot C_01270012 \cdot C_01270013\).
